questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all, I wanted to stay within Europe as it seemed easier to relocate and it was financially more attractive due to the Erasmus grant. Secondly, I have always been drawn towards the Italian culture and loved their food - thus, Italy was an obvious choice for me! I had been told that Bologna was a lively and young student city, and much smaller and less touristy than both Milan and Venice (the two other possible destinations I had in Italy), which made me think of it as the best option among those. I have also found that everything good I heard about Bologna was true!

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky that a friend knew someone who had already acquired an apartment. He got it through someone named Laif - his agency can be contacted through WhatsApp texting +39 39 351 109 36.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is the only possibility. I recommend finding an apartment inside or close to the historic center.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You don't register for the courses in advance - instead you register for the exam. To register for the exam you have to attend the course and they will notify you about the registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My roomates were my source of help - I don't know where they gathered the information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I could register for all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bologna course registration is very different from KU. I recommend getting more courses than required pre accepted as it is usual for the students there to try out many different courses at the beginning of the block / semester. You first officially register for the course about one month before the exam. Also be prepared that this may cause some issues with space in the classrooms, so be there early in the first week.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was the same as I was used to from the masters degree in Economics at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It reminded me a lot of the masters courses at Copenhagen when it came to the lectures - classes of about 30 individuals (but I was told this varied a lot) with mostly the lecturer talking and asking questions. The exercise classes were just mostly repetition of the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Machine Learning for Economists; Field Experiments for Policy Evaluation; Public Economics; Labour Economics and Public Policy; Inequality, Poverty, and Public Policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Field Experiments for Evaluation is an excellent course.

questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected expenses related to the exchange.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was very expensive as I rented a two person room at my own expense.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't end up seeking out cultural and social activities through the University. I didn't find the athletic opportunity for Basketball attractive but I do think there was other great opportunities for other sports at CUSB.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I mostly enjoyed spending time with friends at restaurants, cafes, and going out for drinks.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Rome and the Dolomites and travel a bit around the country. Also just eat at the great restaurants in Bologna - it is much cheaper than eating out in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to adjust - I recommend arriving a week or two before school starts to explore the city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't make any local friends and mostly socialized with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There weren't really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laid back attitude - my everyday life was a lot more laid back.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going as soon as possible, such that you also have the opportunity to go abroad again. Treat the time as part holiday from university as the exams are generally much easier to pass. Enjoy your time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early finding an apartment and if possible find some people at your university you can talk to about the administrative stuff.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I can't answer this question.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
